$$\begin{array}{l} {{P\left( {70 < X < 90} \right)} = {P\left( {\frac{70 - 80}{10} < Z < \frac{90 - 80}{10}} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {70 < X < 90} \right)} = {P\left( {- 1 < Z < 1} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {70 < X < 90} \right)} = {P\left( {Z < 1} \right) - P\left( {Z < - 1} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {70 < X < 90} \right)} = {.8413 - .1587}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {70 < X < 90} \right)} = .6826} \end{array}$$

problem.paragraph: Cholesterol Levels The serum cholesterol levels in milligrams per decaliter (mg/dL) in a current Mediterranean population are found to be normally distributed with a mean of $$160$$ and a standard deviation of $$50$$ . Scientists at the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute consider this pattern ideal for a minimal risk of heart attacks. Find the percentage of the population having blood cholesterol levels between $$160$$ and $$180{mg} \slash {dL}$$ .

solution.paragraph: Let $$X$$ be the normal random variable denoting the serum cholesterol levels in milligrams per deciliter in the current Mediterranean population under consideration. Then the percentage of the population having blood cholesterol levels between $$160$$ and $$180{mg} \slash {dL}$$ is given by $$P(160 < X < 180)$$ . To compute $$P(160 < X < 180)$$ , we use Equation (12) with $$\mu = 160$$ , $$\sigma = 50$$ , $$a = 160$$ , and $$b = 180$$ . We find

$$\begin{array}{l} {{P\left( {160 < X < 180} \right)} = {P\left( {\frac{160 - 160}{50} < Z < \frac{180 - 160}{50}} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {160 < X < 180} \right)} = {P\left( {0 < Z < 0.4} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {160 < X < 180} \right)} = {P\left( {Z < 0.4} \right) - P\left( {Z < 0} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {160 < X < 180} \right)} = {.6554 - .5000}} \\ {\phantom{P\left( {160 < X < 180} \right)} = .1554} \end{array}$$
Thus, approximately $$15.5\%$$ of the population has blood cholesterol levels between $$160$$ and $$180{mg} \slash {dL}$$ .
